title: Delaney Hall Detainee Edwin Lopez-Cornejo Dies; Family Alleges Medical Neglect
excerpt: Edwin Lopez-Cornejo, a 41-year-old Salvadoran man detained at the Delaney Hall facility in Newark, New Jersey, died on August 1, 2026, after suffering a medical emergency in ICE custody. His family alleged he was denied adequate medical treatment despite his chronic illness, triggering protests outside the facility.
content:
Edwin Lopez-Cornejo, 41, a citizen of El Salvador, died at University Hospital in Newark on August 1, 2026, after experiencing a medical emergency at the privately operated Delaney Hall ICE detention facility, run by The GEO Group. He had been detained there for approximately six weeks.

  • Lopez-Cornejo's mother and family alleged he had a chronic illness and was refused adequate medical treatment prior to his emergency.
  • His death was the 22nd reported death in ICE custody in 2026, with the total on pace to exceed the prior-year record of 33 deaths.
  • DHS stated that facility and medical staff responded immediately and called 911, and maintained he received proper medical care.

Delaney Hall had previously been the site of a hunger strike by hundreds of detainees in May 2026 over conditions including contaminated food, extreme temperatures, and overcrowding. Clashes between protesters and masked, armed ICE agents were also documented. New Jersey lawmakers called for an investigation and the ACLU-NJ demanded the facility's closure. Lopez-Cornejo was the third person known to have died after experiencing a medical emergency at Delaney Hall.
source: CNN / CBS New York / New Jersey Monitor
